✨ 6 Skincare Ingredients That Actually Work Skin concerns can feel confusing, but choosing the right ingredient makes it much easier 👀 Blackheads → BHA Oily skin → Niacinamide Dry skin → Ceramide Closed comedones → Adapalene Wrinkles → Retinal Acne → Azelaic acid BHA can help with blackheads and clogged pores, niacinamide is often used for oily skin support, ceramides help support dry skin and the skin barrier, adapalene is commonly used for closed comedones, retinal can help with smoother-looking fine lines, and azelaic acid is often used for acne-prone skin. Some ingredients, like adapalene or retinal, may not be suitable for everyone, so use them carefully and ask a pharmacist or dermatologist if you’re unsure. Morning skincare routine that actually works — and yes, order matters more than you think. Here's the correct sequence to follow every single morning: ✔ Cleanser — skip it if your skin is very dry (over-cleansing is a real thing) ✔ Toner — preps and balances your skin ✔ Vitamin C serum — always apply this one first ✔ Hyaluronic acid serum — lock in that hydration on top ✔ Moisturizer — seal everything in ✔ Sunscreen — non-negotiable, every single day The reason Vitamin C goes before Hyaluronic acid? Vitamin C works best on clean, dry skin at a lower pH — applying it first means better absorption.  Hyaluronic acid then pulls moisture into the skin and keeps it there. Layering them in the right order = you actually get the benefits you're paying for. Most people either skip steps, use the wrong order, or pile everything on at once and wonder why their skin isn't improving.  A consistent, correctly ordered routine beats any expensive product used wrong. Save this so you never second-guess your morning routine again. 💛 #mythbusters #kbeauty #dryskin #skincaresteps #morningskincareroutine
